requirements.text: Behavioural assumptions are based on the Bank's own historical data, and expert judgement used where data are insufficient complies with MRM-STD-023 with its EVE and NII impact quantified.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: Prepayment speeds, deposit volumes and pass-through rates respond to the rate paths of each EVE, NII and SOT scenario rather than being held constant.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: The same behavioural models and parameters are used for EVE, NII, the SOT, ICAAP, hedging and FTP, and any difference is documented and quantified.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: The modelled portfolio is segmented into behaviourally homogeneous segments; NMD segments distinguish at least retail transactional, retail non-transactional, SME and non-financial wholesale deposits.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: For NMD models, balances are split into a volatile and a stable part estimated from historical balance dynamics at a defined confidence level over the modelling horizon.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: For NMD models, volume stability is assessed under stress including rapid digital outflows and rate-driven migration, and stable-part assumptions are at least as conservative as in liquidity stress testing.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: The pass-through model estimates long-term beta and adjustment speed, allows for asymmetry and client-rate floors, and is estimated over rising and falling rate periods.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: The core part is derived from the stable part and pass-through estimate, and replicating portfolio tenors and weights are justified by pass-through behaviour, not by margin targets.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: The average repricing maturity of retail and non-financial wholesale NMD used in the SOT does not exceed five years.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1). Five-year cap per the SOT RTS (Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/856); exact article not cited.

requirements.text: For internal measurement no NMD segment is allocated a tenor above ten years, and the average repricing maturity per segment is reported quarterly to ALCO.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: NMD development data cover at least ten years, or the longest available period, and include at least one period of rising interest rates.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: The mortgage prepayment model uses at least refinancing incentive, loan seasoning, the penalty-free allowance, and relocation and property sale as drivers.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to models covering residential mortgage exposures only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: Full prepayments, partial prepayments and rate resets at the end of the fixed-rate period are modelled or analysed separately.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to models covering residential mortgage exposures only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: EVE and NII projections reflect contractual prepayment penalties, the penalty-free allowance and compensation received on penalty-bearing prepayments.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to models covering residential mortgage exposures only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: Prepayment models are calibrated on at least five years of loan-level history and recalibrated when back-testing shows a structural deviation.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to models covering residential mortgage exposures only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: The pipeline model estimates the take-up of mortgage offers as a function of the market rate change since the offer date and the remaining offer validity.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to models covering residential mortgage exposures only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: Pipeline exposures are included in EVE, NII and the hedging strategy from the offer date using expected take-up under each rate scenario.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to models covering residential mortgage exposures only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: All behavioural models are back-tested at least annually, comparing predicted and realised NMD volumes, deposit rates, prepayment rates per cohort and pipeline take-up.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: Back-testing results are assessed against documented thresholds derived from MV-HB-003, and a red outcome triggers recalibration or an ALCO-approved rationale.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: Sensitivity of EVE and NII to alternative key behavioural assumptions is quantified at least annually and reported to ALCO.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: Model risk from behavioural assumptions is reflected in the ICAAP internal capital for IRRBB based on the sensitivity analysis.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: The SOT is computed at least quarterly for the six EVE and two NII supervisory shock scenarios and compared with the regulatory thresholds and ALCO early-warning levels.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1). EVE threshold of 15% of Tier 1 and NII large-decline test per CRD Art. 98(5) and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/856.

requirements.text: The documentation demonstrates consistent application of behavioural models to the prescribed shock scenarios, including rate floors and post-shock pass-through and prepayment behaviour.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: ALCO approves the key behavioural assumptions (stable and core proportions, betas, replicating portfolio tenors, prepayment calibration) at least annually and on material change.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: Behavioural model changes follow MRM-STD-050, and a change affecting the worst SOT EVE outcome by more than 2% of Tier 1 capital is classified as material.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).

requirements.text: Behavioural model data comply with MRM-STD-022 and the reference data set is documented with the RDS template of MRM-STD-021.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document text authored for the library (ALM-STD-400 v2.1).
